prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create one exceptionally polished native iPhone screen for MagicCuts Pro, a fully paid local sensor and connectivity instrument app. This is a production-quality interface composition, not a marketing poster or website. Flat screen pixels only, portrait aspect matching an iPhone 393 by 852 point viewport, no surrounding device or scene. Respect top status-bar and bottom home-indicator safe areas. Apple Watch face / Apple Compass / Oceanic dive computer standard of disciplined typography, purposeful data geometry, exact alignment, useful information hierarchy. Native SF Pro labels and SF rounded large measurement numerals, never tiny unreadable text. Color world: matte near-black #101315 ground, graphite #22272A wells only when useful, warm white #F4F6F5 text, cool secondary #A5B2B6, measured orange #FF8B52 for the selected reading/control, mint #94D8BE for a labeled passed condition. No gradients, glows, decoration, stock cards, faux metal, 3D hardware, hover affordances, or random circular progress rings. One beautiful dominant measurement geometry; quiet secondary content. Native iOS navigation and tab bar, tab labels Instruments, Sessions, Workflows; Instruments selected. A small legible 'Sample session' label makes all shown data explicitly illustrative. Do not invent unsupported measurements: no Wi-Fi RSSI, distance from Bluetooth signal, temperature sensor, background guarantee or cloud services. Top navigation has title Instruments and a small native settings icon. All actions should look tappable and remain at least 44 points. This is the main unlocked Pro experience. Composition C, 'Comparison Bench': show a native segmented control 'Live / Compare' with Compare selected below navigation. The dominant area is a beautifully engineered pair of compact horizontal instrument rulers, vertically arranged without card boxes, labeled 'Baseline · At desk' and 'Now · By door'. First white rounded numeral '-58' with dBm, orange range band -61 to -55. Second '-74' with dBm, orange range band -80 to -70. Both rulers share exactly the same labeled -100 to -40 scale. A large editorial yet native number in the center '-16 dB' labeled 'Signal change', and a precise small explanatory line 'Weaker than your desk baseline'. Then a shared-axis comparison chart with two distinct traces, baseline in warm white and current orange, labels direct on lines and a real dBm vertical scale, last 20s horizontal scale. A tiny annotation pin 'Door closed' shows where a user marked an event. A clear native primary 'Save comparison' and secondary 'Record again' above bottom tabs. Small 'Sample session' caption. The visual focus is comparing state in the same measurement geometry, not a generic before-after marketing card. All labeling should be honest and useful.
source: Built-in image generation; illustrative interface concept
